{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_8d1ed09512954e169ad4f77f","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Deliver a user's conversation list over the WebSocket protocol\n2\t\n3\tIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#144\n4\tLabels: type:feature, size:M, area:api, area:compliance, epic:extension-points\n5\t\n6\tPart of #35\n7\t\n8\t## Why\n9\t\n10\t#143 gives a consumer `store.listFor(userId)`.\n11\tIt does not give a **client** anything: the browser holding the socket cannot reach the store, so\n12\tevery consumer that wants a history sidebar has to stand up its own authenticated HTTP route over\n13\tthe same data the engine already authenticated on the upgrade. That is a second authorisation\n14\tpath to the same personal data, written once per consumer, each one able to get the ownership\n15\tcheck wrong in its own way — the exact failure #45 went out of its way to avoid for resume.\n16\t\n17\tA consumer may have no such route to extend: an engine deployment behind an api with a session\n18\tstore and no conversation endpoints of its own has nothing to add this to. The engine already knows who is connected and already\n19\treplays a conversation on resume; answering \"which conversations do I have\" over the same socket\n20\tis the smaller surface.\n21\t\n22\t## What to do\n23\t\n24\t- `src/types/messages.ts`, additive only:\n25\t  - `ListConversationsMessage {type: 'list_conversations'; limit?: number; before?: string}` into\n26\t    `IncomingMessage`. There is no user id field, and that is the point: the list is always the\n27\t    connection's authenticated user's.\n28\t  - `ConversationListMessage {type: 'conversation_list'; conversations: ConversationSummary[]}`\n29\t    into `OutgoingMessage`, where `ConversationSummary` is `SessionSummary` with its two times as\n30\t    ISO strings — `Date` does not survive `JSON.stringify` as a `Date`, and the protocol types\n31\t    describe what goes on the wire.\n32\t- `validation.ts`: a `list_conversations` case — `limit`, when present, an integer 1–200;\n33\t  `before`, when present, a string `Date.parse` accepts. Anything else is `INVALID_MESSAGE`, as\n34\t  the two existing cases do it.\n35\t- Handling: `createMessageHandler` takes the session store and the new options alongside the\n36\t  orchestrator (`createServer` already holds both), and answers `list_conversations` on the\n37\t  non-locked path beside `ping` — a history request is not a turn and must not queue behind a\n38\t  streaming answer.\n39\t- The user id comes from `ws.userId`, never from the frame. Add the regression:\n40\t  a frame carrying an extra `userId` of another user is answered with the connecting user's own\n41\t  list.\n42\t- Opt-in: `HalEngineConfig.transport.history?: {enabled: boolean}`, default off, threaded through\n43\t  `createServer`'s options like `resume`. With it off, `list_conversations` is answered with an\n44\t  `error` frame and no list.\n45\t- A store that implements no `listFor` is answered with an `error`, not an empty list: a client\n46\t  that renders \"no conversations\" for a user who has several is a worse answer than one that\n47\t  renders a failure. `ErrorCodes` gains one code for both cases (`UNSUPPORTED`), additive.\n48\t- Picking a conversation needs nothing new: the client reconnects with `?sessionId=<id>`, which\n49\t  #45 already ships with the ownership check and the replay. No in-band switch frame, no second\n50\t  replay path.\n51\t- Specs and docs: extend `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md` (the two frames, their\n52\t  field tables, the authorisation rule) and the conversation-list spec; add § Conversation list\n53\t  to `docs/getting-started.md` by editing `example/full-config.ts` and running `npm run docs:fix`\n54\t  — that listing sits under `<!-- doc-block: example/full-config.ts#full-config -->` and\n55\t  `npm run docs:check` fails a hand-edited block.\n56\t\n57\t## Decisions\n58\t\n59\t- **A frame, not a REST route.** The REST chat routes are demo-only and are not where a consumer is meant to build. The WebSocket is where the caller is\n60\t  already authenticated, once per connection, by the consumer's own `wsAuth`.\n61\t- **Its own opt-in flag, separate from `resume`.** Resume hands a client back a conversation it\n62\t  was already in; a list tells it what else the user has. A deployer who turned on resume did not\n63\t  thereby agree to the second disclosure, and a config that conflates them cannot be audited.\n64\t- **Answered off the per-session lock.** `PerSessionLock` serialises turns (#47). A list request\n65\t  that queued behind a two-minute streaming answer would look broken, and it mutates nothing.\n66\t- **An error, not an empty list, when it cannot be answered.** See above; silence that looks like\n67\t  data is the one failure mode a history view cannot recover from.\n68\t- **Answered when asked, never pushed.** No `conversation_list` arrives unsolicited: a client\n69\t  that just started a conversation knows, and a push would need a fan-out across the sockets a\n70\t  resumed session can be open on.\n71\t- **The frame is accepted by `validateMessage` whether or not the feature is on**, and the\n72\t  handler is what refuses it. This was written before\n92\t      #143's review found that paging on a timestamp alone drops a conversation whenever two\n93\t      share an activity time, so the store's cursor became a composite that accepts an ISO\n94\t      string; a `Date` cannot carry the tie-break. Built as originally written, the transport would have reintroduced the defect the store\n137\t   had just been fixed for.\n138\t2. **`messages.ts` gains four interfaces, not two** — the two frames plus the two payload types\n139\t   they describe.\n140\t3. **`StoreCannotList` is new public surface**, beyond what this issue specified: without it a\n141\t   permanent store misconfiguration cannot be told from a transient failure, in either the client\n142\t   frame or the log.\n143\t\n144\tTwo decisions the criteria did not anticipate:\n145\t\n146\t- **`transport.history` without `transport.resume` is useless, and now says so.** `?sessionId=` is\n147\t  read only when resume is enabled, so a list whose rows cannot be opened is a deployment slip:\n148\t  the engine warns at startup and the documentation says so where it tells a client to reconnect\n149\t  with a row's id. This was written before\n      #143's review found that paging on a timestamp alone drops a conversation whenever two\n      share an activity time, so the store's cursor became a composite that accepts an ISO\n      string; a `Date` cannot carry the tie-break. The handler passes `{limit, before}` with\n      both possibly `undefined` rather than omitting the argument, which is the same call\n- [ ] With `history` absent, the same frame is answered with one `error` frame whose code is\n      `UNSUPPORTED` and no `conversation_list`\n- [ ] With `history: {enabled: true}` against a store implementing no `listFor`, the answer is\n      the same `error` frame, and `grep` shows no code path that sends `conversations: []`\n- [ ] A `listFor` that rejects is answered with one `error` frame whose code is `SERVER_ERROR`\n      and whose message carries no store detail, the socket stays open, and the failure is\n      logged with the session id and no user content. **Added during the build:** a store throwing\n      the new exported `StoreCannotList` is answered `UNSUPPORTED` instead, so an injected\n      collection without a `find` reads as the misconfiguration it is rather than a database\n      that failed\n- [ ] A `list_conversations` sent while a `user_message` is streaming on the same session is\n      answered before that turn's `stream_end` — it does not wait on the lock\n- [ ] A client that takes an id from a `conversation_list` and reconnects with `?sessionId=<id>`\n      receives `resumed: true` and that conversation's replay, with no new transport code: the\n      test exercises the existing #45 path end to end\n- [ ] `ConnectedMessage` is unchanged by this issue\n- [ ] **GDPR.** The protocol spec states that `conversation_list` carries one authenticated\n      user's own conversation metadata and no conversation content, that the user id is taken\n      from the connection and never from the frame, and that `transport.history` is the\n      deployer's decision to make a user's history reachable from the client; `SessionResumeOptions`'\n      retention note is mirrored on the new options type, pointing at #41\n- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` carries an entry under `## [Unreleased]` written for somebody installing the\n      package\n- [ ] The `docs/getting-started.md` change is made in `example/full-config.ts` and the doc\n      regenerated with `npm run docs:fix`, not typed into the markdown\n- [ ] Spec statements carry trailing `([validated by: ...](...#Lnn))` citations, `Status` rows\n      match coverage, and `npm run check:spec-links`, `npm run check:spec-status` and\n      `npm run spec:names` pass\n- [ ] The version bump is MINOR — new optional config, two additive protocol frames, one new\n      error code — and the PR body says so; no migration guide is owed\n- [ ] `npm run verify` passes and the coverage floors for the touched groups hold or rise\n\n## Amendments\n\nThree things changed between writing this issue and building it, each marked in the criterion it\naffects:\n\n1. **`before` is a cursor, not a timestamp.** #143's review found that paging on `updatedAt` alone\n   silently drops a conversation when two share an activity time. The store's cursor became\n   `{updatedAt, sessionId}`, so the frame carries both halves and the validator refuses one half\n   alone. Built as originally written, the transport would have reintroduced the defect the store\n   had just been fixed for.\n2. **`messages.ts` gains four interfaces, not two** — the two frames plus the two payload types\n   they describe.\n3. **`StoreCannotList` is new public surface**, beyond what this issue specified: without it a\n   permanent store misconfiguration cannot be told from a transient failure, in either the client\n   frame or the log.\n\nTwo decisions the criteria did not anticipate:\n\n- **`transport.history` without `transport.resume` is useless, and now says so.** `?sessionId=` is\n  read only when resume is enabled, so a list whose rows cannot be opened is a deployment slip:\n  the engine warns at startup and the documentation says so where it tells a client to reconnect\n  with a row's id. Refusing to start was considered and rejected as too blunt for a library.\n- **The conversation the connection is in is listed like any other**, so a fresh connect sees a row\n  of its own holding no entries. Filtering it out was rejected: it is a real conversation the user\n  is in, and it is their newest the moment they send anything.\n\n## Tech notes\n\nDepends on #143: without `listFor` there is\nnothing to send.\n\nKey paths: `src/types/messages.ts`, `src/types/session.ts` (`ErrorCodes`),\n`src/transport/ws/{validation,messageHandler,sender}.ts`, `src/transport/createServer.ts`,\n`src/config.ts`, `example/full-config.ts`, `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md`.\n\nOut of scope: a preview or title on the summaries (its own issue); deleting a conversation from\nthe client, which would put an erasure primitive on the wire and needs its own authorisation\ndecision; paging state held server-side — the client pages with `before`; an operator view of\nanother user's conversations, which is an authorisation question of its own; and live sync between open tabs,\nwhich #124 ruled out.\n\nRefs #143, #145, #41, #45, #47, #124\n\n\n\n\n","numLines":174,"startLine":1,"totalLines":174}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_8d1ed09512954e169ad4f77f","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{once} from 'node:events';\nimport type {AddressInfo} from 'node:net';\nimport {WebSocket} from 'ws';\nimport type {Express} from 'express';\nimport {createServer} from './createServer.js';\nimport {InMemorySessionStore} from '../infrastructure/stores/inMemorySessionStore.js';\nimport type {ChatOrchestrator} from '../orchestration/chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport type {MessageChunk} from '../types/ai.js';\nimport type {ConnectedMessage} from '../types/messages.js';\nimport type {SessionEntry} from '../types/session.js';\nimport type {SessionStore} from '../types/sessionStore.js';\nimport {setLogger} from '../shared/logger.js';\n\n// Real upgrades over a real socket: what a reconnect is sent is the contract, and no double can observe it.\n\ninterface Frame {\n  type: string;\n  sessionId?: string;\n  resumed?: boolean;\n  entryCount?: number;\n  resumeFailure?: string;\n  index?: number;\n  entry?: SessionEntry;\n}\n\nconst NEVER_ISSUED = '0f1e2d3c-4b5a-4968-8776-655443322110';\nconst RESUME_ON: SessionResumeOptions = {enabled: true};\nconst LATEST_ON: SessionResumeOptions = {enabled: true, latest: true};\nconst HALF_ANSWER: SessionEntry = {\n  role: 'assistant',\n  content: 'half',\n  timestamp: '2026-09-30T08:00:01.000Z',\n  isStreaming: true,\n};\n\n// A tool's suppression lands while the answer is still open, as when a provider ends a tool round with no stop.\nconst suppressingMidAnswer: ChatOrchestrator = {\n  processMessage: async () => 'before after',\n  async *processMessageStream(): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n    yield {type: 'text', text: 'before'};\n    yield {type: 'suppress_output'} as unknown as MessageChunk;\n    yield {type: 'text', text: ' after'};\n    yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\n  },\n};\n\nconst servers: Array<ReturnType<typeof createServer>> = [];\nconst clients: WebSocket[] = [];\n\nconst eventually = async (check: () => boolean): Promise<void> => {\n  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 50 && !check(); attempt++) await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 10));\n};\n\n// Silenced for the whole file: the server logs every connection and close, and these tests read frames, not logs.\nbeforeAll(() => {\n  setLogger({debug: () => undefined, info: () => undefined, warn: () => undefined, error: () => undefined});\n});\n\nafterAll(() => {\n  setLogger();\n});\n\n// Each server sees its sockets close before it stops, so no close is logged after the logger above is restored.\nafterEach(async () => {\n  for (const client of clients.splice(0)) client.terminate();\n  for (const hal of servers.splice(0)) {\n    const {wss} = hal;\n    await eventually(() => wss.clients.size === 0);\n    await hal.stop();\n  }\n});\n\n// The authenticated user is read per upgrade, so one test can reconnect as someone else.\nconst startEngine = async (\n  store: SessionStore,\n  resume?: SessionResumeOptions,\n  orchestrator: ChatOrchestrator = answeringOrchestrator\n) => {\n  const auth = {userId: 'u1'};\n  const connects: Array<{sessionId: string; resumed: boolean}> = [];\n  const disconnected: string[] = [];\n  const hal = createServer({\n    app: (() => undefined) as unknown as Express,\n    wsAuth: async () => ({id: auth.userId}),\n    sessionStore: store,\n    orchestrator,\n    resume,\n    onConnect: (session, {resumed}) => void connects.push({sessionId: session.sessionId, resumed}),\n    onDisconnect: sessionId => void disconnected.push(sessionId),\n  });\n  // Resolves once the server itself has seen its first socket close, which the client's own close can precede.\n  const firstServerClose = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    hal.wss.once('connection', socket => socket.once('close', () => resolve()));\n  });\n  await hal.start(0);\n  servers.push(hal);\n  const {port} = hal.server.address() as AddressInfo;\n  return {auth, connects, disconnected, firstServerClose, base: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/hal/ws`};\n};\n\nconst open = (url: string, token = 't'): WebSocket => {\n  const client = new WebSocket(url, [HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL, token]);\n  clients.push(client);\n  return client;\n};\n\n// One question answered and the socket closed, returning the id the connected frame announced.\nconst firstTurn = async (base: string): Promise<string> => {\n  const client = open(base);\n  let sessionId = '';\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') sessionId = frame.sessionId ?? '';\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'user_message', content: 'hello'}));\n      if (frame.type === 'stream_end') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  client.close();\n  await once(client, 'close');\n  return sessionId;\n};\n\n// A ping sent on connect is a barrier: its pong can only follow every frame the replay wrote.\nconst connectAndSettle = async (url: string, token?: string): Promise<Frame[]> => {\n  const client = open(url, token);\n  const frames: Frame[] = [];\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      frames.push(frame);\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1}));\n      if (frame.type === 'pong') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  return frames;\n};\n\nconst upserts = (frames: Frame[]) =>\n  frames.filter(frame => frame.type === 'entry_upsert').map(({index, entry}) => ({index, entry}));\n\nconst shapeOf = (frames: Frame[]) => ({\n  keys: Object.keys(frames[0]).sort(),\n  resumed: frames[0].resumed,\n  resumeFailure: frames[0].resumeFailure,\n  types: frames.map(frame => frame.type),\n});\n\nconst deferredRelease = () => {\n  let release = (): void => undefined;\n  const until = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    release = resolve;\n  });\n  return {until, release: () => release()};\n};\n\n// Each stored conversation holds one user entry, sent at the given time and reading as its own id.\nconst storeWith = (conversations: Array<[sessionId: string, userId: string, sentAt: string]>): InMemorySessionStore => {\n  const store = new InMemorySessionStore();\n  for (const [sessionId, userId, sentAt] of conversations) {\n    const {entries} = store.create(sessionId, userId);\n    entries.push({role: 'user', content: sessionId, timestamp: sentAt});\n  }\n  return store;\n};\n\n// A store with only the required members, so an optional one can be added, replaced or left out per test.\nconst delegatingTo = (inner: InMemorySessionStore): SessionStore => ({\n  create: (sessionId, userId, options) => inner.create(sessionId, userId, options),\n  get: sessionId => inner.get(sessionId),\n  delete: sessionId => inner.delete(sessionId),\n  count: () => inner.count(),\n  clear: () => inner.clear(),\n});\n\ndescribe('resuming a conversation on reconnect', () => {\n  it('with resume absent, answers a reconnect naming the first id with a new id and no replay', async () => {\n    const {base} = await startEngine(new InMemorySessionStore());\n    const first = await firstTurn(base);\n\n    const frames = await connectAndSettle(`${base}?sessionId=${first}`);\n\n    expect({newId: frames[0].sessionId !== first, shape: shapeOf(frames)}).toEqual({\n      newId: true,\n      shape: {\n        keys: ['examplePrompts', 'message', 'sessionId', 'type'],\n        resumed: undefined,\n        types: ['connected', 'pong'],\n      },\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('with resume on, answers the owner reconnecting with resumed true, entryCount 2 and both stored entries', async () => {\n    const store = new connectAndSettle(`${base}?sessionId=${first}`);\n\n    const stored = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify((await store.get(first))?.entries)) as SessionEntry[];\n    expect({connected: frames[0], replay: entry: stored[1]},\n      ],\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('answers another user naming the id exactly as it answers an id that was never issued', async () => {\n    const {auth, base} = await ['examplePrompts', 'message', 'resumeFailure', 'resumed', 'sessionId', 'type'],\n      resumed: false,\n      resumeFailure: 'unknown',\n      types: ['connected', 'pong'],\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('never adopts a requested id as a key: one session, under the id the server minted', async () => {\n    const store = new InMemorySessionStore();\n    const {base} = await startEngine(store, resumed: {sessionId: 'known', resumed: true, entryCount: 1},\n      fresh: {resumed: false},\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('replays a suppressed entry as a skip, so the client never sees text a tool const replayed = JSON.stringify(frames);\n    expect({\n      types: frames.map(({type, index}) => (index === undefined ? type : `${type} ${index}`)),\n      leaked: ['before', 'after'].filter(word => => inner.clear(),\n      evict: sessionId => {\n        evicted.push(sessionId);\n        return inner.evict(sessionId);\n      },\n    };\n    const {base, firstServerClose} = await expect(frames[0]).toMatchObject({sessionId: 'older', resumed: true});\n  });\n\n  it(\"starts a new session when the store's latestFor answers another user's session, throws, or is absent\", async () target.left : target;\n58\t    return pattern.type === \"ObjectPattern\" ? pattern : null;\n59\t}\n60\tfunction typeLiteralFlagNames(pattern) {\n61\t    const annotation = pattern.typeAnnotation?.typeAnnotation;\n62\t    if (annotation?.type !== \"TSTypeLiteral\") {\n63\t        return [];\n64\t    }\n65\t    return annotation.members\n66\t        .filter((member) => member.type === \"TSPropertySignature\")\n67\t        .filter((member) => isBooleanTypeNode(member.typeAnnotation?.typeAnnotation))\n68\t        .map((member) => member.key.name);\n69\t}\n70\tfunction defaultedFlagNames(pattern) {\n71\t    return pattern.properties\n72\t        .filter((property) => property.type === \"Property\")\n73\t        .filter((property) => property.value.type === \"AssignmentPattern\" &&\n74\t        isBooleanLiteral(property.value.right))\n75\t        .map((property) => property.key.name);\n76\t}\n77\tfunction destructuredFlagNames(pattern) {\n78\t    return [\n79\t        ...new Set([\n80\t            ...typeLiteralFlagNames(pattern),\n81\t            ...defaultedFlagNames(pattern),\n82\t        ]),\n83\t    ];\n84\t}\n85\tfunction flagPropertyValue(property) {\n86\t    if (property.type !== \"Property\") {\n87\t        return null;\n88\t    }\n89\t    return isBooleanLiteral(property.value) ? tailLength\n        : null;\n}\nfunction guardDescriptor(node) {\n    const tailLength = wrappedTailLength(node);\n    if (tailLength === null)\n        return null;\n    return { node, messageId: \"flipToGuard\", data: { tail: String(tailLength) } };\n}\nexport default {\n    meta: {\n        type: \"suggestion\",\n        fixable: \"code\",\n        docs: {\n            description: \"Guard clauses over else branches and wrapped tails: de-nest an else after a terminating if, split a non-terminating if/else into two ifs, and flip an if that wraps the whole happy path.\",\n        },\n        messages: {\n            unnecessaryElse: \"The if branch {{how}}, so this else only nests — de-nest its statements to follow the if.\",\n            splitIntoTwoIfs: \"No else branches: split into two ifs — `if (x)` and `if (!x)` — or restructure so the first branch returns.\",\n            flipToGuard: \"The happy path is wrapped in this if while {{tail}} statement(s) dangle after it — flip to `if (!(…))` guarding the tail and let the happy path run flat.\",\n        },\n        schema: [],\n    },\n    create(context) {\n        const sourceCode = context.sourceCode;\n        return {\n            IfStatement(node) {\n                const descriptor = node.alternate\n                    ? {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_2d1c837677914552b2bbf036","type":"tool_result","content":"import type {AddressInfo} from 'node:net';\nimport {WebSocket} from 'ws';\nimport type {Express} from 'express';\nimport {createServer} from './createServer.js';\nimport type {HalServer, HalServerOptions} from './createServer.js';\nimport {HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL} from './ws/subprotocol.js';\nimport type {ChatOrchestrator} from '../orchestration/chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport type {MessageChunk} from '../types/ai.js';\nimport type {ChatSession} from '../types/session.js';\nimport type {SessionStore} from '../types/sessionStore.js';\n\n// Shared by the suites that need a real upgrade over a real socket, which no double can stand in for.\n\nconst servers: Array<{stop: () => Promise<void>}> = [];\nconst clients: WebSocket[] = [];\n\n/** An orchestrator that answers once and stops, which is what commits the turn's assistant entry. */\nexport const answeringOrchestrator: ChatOrchestrator = {\n  processMessage: async () => 'hi',\n  async *processMessageStream(): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n    yield {type: 'text', text: 'hi'};\n    yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\n  },\n};\n\n/** Starts an engine on an ephemeral port and returns the URL a client should open. */\nexport async function startEngine(\n  sessionStore: SessionStore,\n  onDisconnect?: (sessionId: string) => void\n): Promise<string> {\n  const {url} = await startEngineWith({sessionStore, onDisconnect});\n  return url;\n}\n\n/** Starts an engine with whatever a suite overrides, returning the server itself beside the URL a client should open. */\nexport async function startEngineWith(\n  options: Partial<HalServerOptions> & Pick<HalServerOptions, 'sessionStore'>\n): Promise<{url: string; hal: HalServer}> {\n  const hal = createServer({\n    app: (() => undefined) as unknown as Express,\n    wsAuth: async () => ({id: 'u1'}),\n    orchestrator: answeringOrchestrator,\n    ...options,\n  });\n  await hal.start(0);\n  servers.push(hal);\n  const {port} = hal.server.address() as AddressInfo;\n  return {url: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/hal/ws/c1`, hal};\n}\n\n/** Opens a client that the suite's teardown will close, whether its test passed or failed. */\nexport function connectClient(url: string, token = 't'): WebSocket {\n  const client = new WebSocket(url, [HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL, token]);\n  clients.push(client);\n  return client;\n}\n\n/** A promise a test settles by hand, to hold a stream or a hook at a point of its choosing. */\nexport function deferred(): {until: Promise<void>; release: () => void} {\n  let release = (): void => undefined;\n  const until = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    release = resolve;\n  });\n  return {until, release};\n}\n\n/** Resolves with every frame type seen up to and including the first `until` frame. */\nexport function framesUntil(client: WebSocket, until: string): Promise<string[]> {\n  const seen: string[] = [];\n  return new Promise<string[]>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const {type} = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as {type: string};\n      seen.push(type);\n      if (type === until) resolve(seen);\n    });\n  });\n}\n\n/** Opens a client that asks one question the moment the socket opens, resolving on the first `until` frame. */\nexport function askOnOpen(\n  url: string,\n  {until = 'stream_end', token}: {until?: string; token?: string} = {}\n): {client: WebSocket; finished: Promise<string[]>} {\n  const client = connectClient(url, token);\n  const finished = framesUntil(client, until);\n  client.on('open', () => client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'user_message', content: 'hello'})));\n  return {client, finished};\n}\n\n/** The session id the client's `connected` frame announces, read after the fact; attach it before any frame arrives. */\nexport function announcedId(client: WebSocket): () => string {\n  let sessionId = '';\n  client.on('message', raw => {\n    const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as {type: string; sessionId?: string};\n    if (frame.type === 'connected') sessionId = frame.sessionId ?? '';\n  });\n  return () => sessionId;\n}\n\n/** Tears every socket and server down, so a red test reports instead of hanging the run. */\nexport async function stopEngines(): Promise<void> {\n  for (const client of clients.splice(0)) client.terminate();\n  for (const hal of servers.splice(0)) await hal.stop();\n}\n\n/** The one session a store holds, for asserting what survived a close. */\nexport async function onlySession(store: SessionStore, sessionId: string): Promise<ChatSession | undefined> {\n  return (await store.get(sessionId)) as ChatSession | undefined;\n}\n=== {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_a02a039301b540978a817ef1","type":"tool_result","content":"specs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md:8:Resume gets a client back into one conversation: the id it names, or the user's most recently active one. Neither tells it which conversations exist, and every other member of `SessionStore` answers about a session the caller can already name, so a consumer wanting to offer a conversation list had to query the collection behind the engine's back, against a document shape and a key the engine owns. `listFor` answers the list instead, as summaries rather than sessions. **GDPR.** A summary is personal data — that a user held a conversation, and when — so it carries no conversation content, it is filtered to one user by the query rather than in application code afterwards, and the retention bound stays the consumer's, through the store's `maxAgeMs` and erasure methods and re-cinq/HALEngine#41.\nspecs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md:13:- `listFor` is optional, like `latestFor` and `lookup` before it: a store written against the five original members still satisfies the interface, and both shipped stores implement it ([validated by: leaves a store with only the five original members satisfying the interface beside both shipped ones](../../src/infrastructure/stores/sessionStoreListSignature.test.ts#L11)).\nspecs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md:55:- They page identically through the documented call, `listFor(userId, {limit, before: rows.at(-1)})`, a page at a time until a page comes back empty ([validated by: page the same way through the documented call, ignored ([validated by: answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L93)).\nspecs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md:75:- A store without `listFor` answers `{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}`, and a throwing `listFor` logs an error on the `ws` category and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}` ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L134)).\nspecs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md:76:- The validator accepts an optional non-negative {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_7aa2d1292d5646c7ace39a4e","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport http from 'http';\n2\timport {WebSocketServer} from 'ws';\n3\timport type {Express} from 'express';\n4\timport type {WsAuthenticator} from '../types/auth.js';\n5\timport type {SessionStore} from '../types/sessionStore.js';\n6\timport type {ChatOrchestrator} from '../orchestration/chatOrchestrator.js';\n7\timport type {ToolRegistry} from '../orchestration/tools/registry.js';\n8\timport {createUpgradeHandler, createConnectionHandler, ExtWebSocket} from './ws/connectionHandler.js';\n9\timport {createMessageHandler} from './ws/messageHandler.js';\n10\timport {selectSubprotocol} from './ws/subprotocol.js';\n11\timport type {ConnectInfo, SessionResumeOptions} from './ws/sessionResume.js';\n12\timport {log} from '../shared/logger.js';\n13\t\n14\texport interface HalServerOptions {\n15\t  app: Express;\n16\t  wsAuth: WsAuthenticator;\n17\t  sessionStore: SessionStore;\n18\t  orchestrator: ChatOrchestrator;\n19\t  toolRegistry?: ToolRegistry;\n20\t  basePath?: string;\n21\t  port?: number;\n22\t  heartbeatIntervalMs?: number;\n23\t  onConnect?: (session: import('../types/session.js').ChatSession, connection: ConnectInfo) => void | Promise<void>;\n24\t  onDisconnect?: (sessionId: string) => void | Promise<void>;\n25\t  resume?: SessionResumeOptions;\n26\t}\n27\t\n28\texport interface HalServer {\n29\t  server: http.Server;\n30\t  wss: WebSocketServer;\n31\t  start: (port?: number) => Promise<void>;\n32\t  stop: () => Promise<void>;\n33\t}\n34\t\n35\texport function createServer(options: HalServerOptions): HalServer {\n36\t  const basePath = options.basePath ?? '/hal';\n37\t\n38\t  const wss = new WebSocketServer({\n39\t    noServer: true,\n40\t    handleProtocols: selectSubprotocol,\n41\t  });\n42\t\n43\t  const handleMessage = createMessageHandler(options.orchestrator);\n44\t  const examplePrompts = options.toolRegistry?.getExamplePrompts() ?? from '../../types/session.js';\nimport {ErrorCodes} from '../../types/session.js';\nimport {sendError} from './sender.js';\nimport {isValidWsPath, rejectSocket, parseWsData, sessionIdFromUpgrade, newSessionRequested} from './helpers.js';\nimport {credentialFromSubprotocol} from './subprotocol.js';\nimport {replayEntries, resumableSession, resumeFields} from './sessionResume.js';\nimport type {ConnectInfo, SessionResumeOptions} from './sessionResume.js';\nimport {log} from '../../shared/logger.js';\n\nexport interface ExtWebSocket extends WebSocket {\n  isAlive: boolean;\n  userId: string | number;\n  workspaceId?: string | number;\n  authHeaders?: {\n    cookie?: string;\n    authorization?: string;\n    host?: string;\n  };\n  requestedSessionId?: string;\n  startNewSession?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface ConnectionHandlerDeps {\n  wsAuth: WsAuthenticator;\n  sessionStore: SessionStore;\n  /** `signal` is the connection's own, aborted when its socket closes (specs/hal-engine-abandon-on-close/spec.md). */\n  handleMessage: (\n    ws: WebSocket,\n    session: import('../../types/session.js').ChatSession,\n    rawMessage: unknown,\n    signal?: AbortSignal\n  ) => Promise<void>;\n  basePath: string;\n  onConnect?: (session: import('../../types/session.js').ChatSession, connection: ConnectInfo) => void | Promise<void>;\n  onDisconnect?: (sessionId: string) => void | Promise<void>;\n  resume?: SessionResumeOptions;\n}\nexport function createUpgradeHandler(wss: WebSocketServer, deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps) {\n  return function handleUpgrade(request: IncomingMessage, socket: Duplex, head: Buffer): void {\n    // Nothing may throw out of this listener: the `upgrade` event has no catch above it, so a throw ends the process.\n    if (!request.headers.host || !isValidWsPath(request.url || '', deps.basePath)) {\n      rejectSocket(socket, '400 Bad Request');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    authenticate(deps.wsAuth, request)\n      .then(user => {\n        if (!user) {\n          rejectSocket(socket, '401 Unauthorized');\n          return;\n        }\n\n        wss.handleUpgrade(request, socket, head, ws => {\n          const extWs = ws as ExtWebSocket;\n          extWs.userId = user.id;\n          extWs.workspaceId = user['workspaceId'] as string | number | undefined;\n          extWs.authHeaders = {\n            cookie: request.headers.cookie,\n            authorization: request.headers.authorization || bearerFromWebSocketProtocol(request),\n            host: (request.headers['x-forwarded-host'] as string | undefined) ?? request.headers.host,\n          };\n          extWs.isAlive = true;\n          if (deps.resume?.enabled) {\n            extWs.requestedSessionId = sessionIdFromUpgrade(request.url || '', deps.basePath);\n            extWs.startNewSession = newSessionRequested(request.url || '', deps.basePath);\n          }\n          wss.emit('connection', extWs, request);\n        });\n      })\n      .catch((error: unknown) => {\n        // The type alone: an authenticator's message can carry the credential it was checking.\n        log.error('ws', 'authenticator failed', {errorType: error instanceof Error ? error.name : typeof error});\n        rejectSocket(socket, '500 Internal Server Error');\n      });\n  };\n}\n\n// Async, so a synchronous throw becomes a rejection (answered 500) and a user returned without a promise still resolves.\nasync function authenticate(wsAuth: WsAuthenticator, request: IncomingMessage): Promise<AuthenticatedUser | null> {\n  return wsAuth(request);\n}\n\nfunction bearerFromWebSocketProtocol(req: IncomingMessage): string | undefined {\n  const token = credentialFromSubprotocol(req.headers['sec-websocket-protocol']);\n  return token ? `Bearer ${token}` : undefined;\n}\n\nexport function createConnectionHandler(deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps, examplePrompts: string[]) {\n  return function handleConnection(ws: ExtWebSocket): void {\n    // The listener stays synchronous: an async one rejects into the emitter, and node ends the process on that.\n    openSession(deps, examplePrompts, ws).catch((error: unknown) => {\n      log.error('ws', 'connection setup failed', {error: messageOf(error)});\n      // Resumed before closing: a paused socket never reads the close frame it would be waiting for.\n      ws.resume();\n      ws.close(1011, 'Connection setup failed');\n    });\n  };\n}\n\n// The sockets open on each session, oldest first: a resumed session can be open on more than one at once.\nconst openSockets = new WeakMap<ChatSession, ExtWebSocket[]>();\n\nasync function openSession(deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps, examplePrompts: string[], ws: ExtWebSocket): Promise<void> {\n  // A requested id is never adopted for a new session: that would be session fixation.\n  let sessionId = uuidv4();\n  const state = {closed: false, settled: false, notified: false, delivered: false};\n  const held: {session?: ChatSession; socket: ExtWebSocket} = {socket: ws};\n  // One per connection, not per message or session: a close abandons the turn in flight and every message queued behind it.\n  const connection = new AbortController();\n\n  ws.on('error', (error: Error) => {\n    log.error('ws', 'connection error', {sessionId, error: error.message});\n  });\n\n  ws.on('pong', () => {\n    ws.isAlive = true;\n  });\n\n  ws.on('close', () => {\n    // First, so the turn stops before the session is torn down and before onDisconnect.\n    connection.abort();\n    state.closed = true;\n    log.info('ws', 'disconnected', {sessionId});\n    if (state.settled) endSession(deps, sessionId, state, held);\n  });\n\n  // Paused across the await so a frame arriving before the message listener exists is buffered, not dropped.\n  ws.pause();\n\n  const outcome = await resumableSession(deps.sessionStore, ws, deps.resume);\n  const resumed = outcome.session;\n  if (resumed) sessionId = resumed.sessionId;\n  const session = resumed ?? (await createSession(deps, sessionId, ws));\n  state.settled = true;\n\n  if (session === undefined) {\n    // Resumed before closing: ws.close() on a paused socket waits for a close frame it can never read.\n    ws.resume();\n    ws.close(1011, 'Session store unavailable');\n    return;\n  }\n\n  // A new session is this socket's from the start; a resumed one only once this socket is known to be open.\n  if (!resumed) join(session, ws);\n\n  if (state.closed) {\n    // Held first: a store that implements no evict still holds this session, and it carries the caller's credentials.\n    held.session = session;\n    await evictUnlessResumed(deps, sessionId, resumed);\n    endSession(deps, sessionId, state, held);\n    ws.resume();\n    return;\n  }\n\n  if (resumed) join(resumed, ws);\n  held.session = session;\n\n  log.info('ws', 'connected', {sessionId, userId: ws.userId});\n\n  const connected: ConnectedMessage = {\n    type: 'connected',\n    sessionId,\n    message: 'Connected to HAL Engine',\n    examplePrompts,\n    ...resumeFields(deps.resume, outcome),\n  };\n  // A socket that died between the check above and this frame must not leave the session it was created for behind.\n  try {\n    ws.send(JSON.stringify(connected));\n    if (resumed) replayEntries(ws, resumed);\n  } catch (error) {\n    log.error('ws', 'connected frame failed', {sessionId, error: messageOf(error)});\n    await evictUnlessResumed(deps, sessionId, resumed);\n    endSession(deps, sessionId, state, held);\n    ws.resume();\n    ws.close(1011, 'Connection setup failed');\n    return;\n  }\n\n  state.delivered = true;\n\n  // Deferred, not inline: a synchronous throw in the `connection` listener corrupts an already-upgraded socket.\n\n  // A microtask, not setImmediate: it drains before the loop delivers any inbound frame on this socket.\n  queueMicrotask(() =>\n    runHook('onConnect', sessionId, () => deps.onConnect?.(session, {resumed: resumed !== undefined}))\n  );\n\n  ws.on('message', (frame: Buffer | string) => {\n    const parsed = parseWsData(frame);\n    if (parsed === null) {\n      sendError(ws, ErrorCodes.INVALID_FORMAT, 'Invalid JSON');\n      return;\n    }\n    log.info('ws', 'message received', {sessionId, type: (parsed as Record<string, unknown>).type as string});\n    deps.handleMessage(ws, session, parsed, connection.signal);\n  });\n\n  ws.resume();\n}\n\n// Joined as the newest socket on the session, which carries this upgrade's credentials from here on.\nfunction join(session: ChatSession, ws: ExtWebSocket): void {\n  openSockets.set(session, [...(openSockets.get(session) ?? []), ws]);\n  session.authHeaders = ws.authHeaders;\n}\n\n// `undefined` rather than a throw: one store failure closes one socket instead of ending the process.\nasync function createSession(\n  deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps,\n  sessionId: string,\n  ws: ExtWebSocket\n): Promise<ChatSession | undefined> {\n  try {\n    return await deps.sessionStore.create(sessionId, ws.userId, {\n      authHeaders: ws.authHeaders,\n      workspaceId: ws.workspaceId,\n    });\n  } catch (error) {\n    log.error('ws', 'session create failed', {userId: ws.userId, error: messageOf(error)});\n    sendError(ws, ErrorCodes.SERVER_ERROR, 'Could not start a session');\n    return undefined;\n  }\n}\n\n// The close path erases nothing: the conversation outlives its socket, and `onDisconnect` is the consumer's seam.\nfunction endSession(\n  deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps,\n  sessionId: string,\n  state: {notified: boolean; delivered: boolean},\n  held: {session?: ChatSession; socket: ExtWebSocket}\n): void {\n  if (state.notified) return;\n  state.notified = true;\n\n  if (held.session) leave(held.session, held.socket);\n\n  // Only for a session the consumer was actually handed: onDisconnect is the other half of onConnect, not of a socket.\n  if (!state.delivered) return;\n\n  runHook('onDisconnect', sessionId, () => deps.onDisconnect?.(sessionId));\n}\n\n// The newest socket still open lends the session its credentials; with none left, nothing keeps them or a closed socket.\nfunction leave(session: ChatSession, ws: ExtWebSocket): void {\n  const open = openSockets.get(session) ?? [];\n  if (!open.includes(ws)) return;\n  const remaining = open.filter(socket => socket !== ws);\n  const newest = remaining.at(-1);\n  if (newest === undefined) {\n    openSockets.delete(session);\n    session.authHeaders = undefined;\n    return;\n  }\n  openSockets.set(session, remaining);\n  session.authHeaders = newest.authHeaders;\n}\n\n// Never a resumed session: evict erases, and a resumed session holds the conversation being rejoined.\nasync function evictUnlessResumed(\n  deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps,\n  sessionId: string,\n  resumed: ChatSession | undefined\n): Promise<void> {\n  if (!resumed) await evictSession(deps, sessionId);\n}\n\n// Only for a session no client ever received: it has no entries and nothing to migrate.\nasync function evictSession(deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps, sessionId: string): Promise<void> {\n  try {\n    await deps.sessionStore.evict?.(sessionId);\n  } catch (error) {\n    log.error('ws', 'session evict failed', {sessionId, error: messageOf(error)});\n  }\n}\n\n// Consumer hooks are fire-and-forget: the engine never awaits one and never lets one take the connection down.\nfunction runHook(name: string, sessionId: string, call: () => void | Promise<void>): void {\n  try {\n    // Promise.resolve also absorbs a thenable from another realm, where `instanceof Promise` is false.\n    void Promise.resolve(call()).catch((error: unknown) => logHookFailure(name, sessionId, error));\n  } catch (error) {\n    logHookFailure(name, sessionId, error);\n  }\n}\n\nfunction logHookFailure(name: string, sessionId: string, error: unknown): void {\n  log.error('ws', `${name} hook failed`, {sessionId, error: messageOf(error)});\n}\n\nfunction messageOf(error: unknown): string {\n  if (typeof error === 'object' && error !== null && 'message' in error) return String(error.message);\n  return String(error);\n}\n","numLines":302,"startLine":1,"totalLines":302}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_fdfe3aeb88d24e69bab64d93","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

read.\nconst wire = (sent: OutgoingMessage[]): string[] =>\n  sent.map(frame => {\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_upsert') {\n      const content = 'content' in frame.entry ? frame.entry.content : '';\n      return `upsert ${frame.index} ${frame.entry.role} ${JSON.stringify(content)}`;\n    }\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_delta') return `delta ${frame.index} ${JSON.stringify(frame.delta)}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_commit') return `commit ${frame.index}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_skip') return `skip ${frame.index}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'error') return `error ${frame.code}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'pong') return `pong ${frame.timestamp}`;\n    return frame.type;\n  });\n\nconst text = (value: string): MessageChunk => ({type: 'text', text: value});\nconst {chunks: number; until: Promise<void>};\n}\n\nconst harness = (chunks: MessageChunk[], {failWith, pauseAfter}: StreamScript = {}) => {\n  const sent: OutgoingMessage[] = [];\n  const ws = {send: (raw: an import above a suite moves every test below\n// it, and the citation silently lands on a different, still-valid declaration. The name is what the\n// author meant, so the name is what the citation records and the line becomes a derived pointer this\n// script repairs. The `#Lnn` stays because the lint rule and the coverage job both index by it, and a\n// citation without one marks the whole file covered rather than one test.\nimport {readFileSync, writeFileSync} [^\\]]*)?\\]\\((?<path>[^)#\\s]+)#L\\d+\\)/g;\n// `xit`, `xdescribe` and `.skip` declare a test that never runs, which validates nothing.\nconst DECLARATION = return;\n  }\n  sendStreamEnd(ws);\n}\n\nasync function answerUserMessage(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  orchestrator: ChatOrchestrator,\n  validation: ValidationResult,\n  signal: null,\n    suppressOutput: false,\n    sentAssistantIndices: [],\n  };\n\n  let textChunkCount = 0;\n\n  try {\n    for await (const chunk of orchestrator.processMessageStream(session, {signal})) {\n (chunk.type === 'text') return textChunkCount + 1;\n\n  if (textChunkCount > 0) {\n    log.debug('stream', `received ${textChunkCount} text chunks`);\n  }\n\n  if (chunk.type === 'tool_result') {\n    log.debug('stream', 'tool_result chunk', {\n      messageCount: chunk.clientMessages.length,\n      types: chunk.clientMessages.map(m => m.type),\n    });\n    return 0;\n  }\n\n  log.debug('stream', 'chunk', {type: chunk.type});\n  return 0;\n}\n\nfunction processChunk(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  state: StreamState,\n  parser: ThinkingTagParser,\n  chunk: MessageChunk\n): void {\n  if (chunk.type === 'text') return processTextChunk(ws, session, state, parser, chunk.text);\n  if (chunk.type === 'tool_use') return processToolUseChunk(ws, session, chunk.toolCall);\n  if (chunk.type === 'tool_result') return processToolResultChunk(ws, chunk.clientMessages);\n  if (chunk.type === 'suppress_output') return processSuppressChunk(ws, session, state);\n  if (chunk.type === 'stop') return processStopChunk(ws, session, state, parser);\n}\n\nfunction processTextChunk(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  state: StreamState,\n  parser: ThinkingTagParser,\n  text: string\n): void {\n  const segments = parser.push(text);\n  for (const segment of segments) {\n    handleTextSegment(ws, session, state, segment);\n  }\n}\n\nfunction handleTextSegment(ws: WebSocket, segment.content);\n    return;\n  }\n  commitAndClear(ws, session, state, 'thinkingIndex');\n  streamSegment(ws, session, state, 'assistantIndex', createAssistantEntry, const isNew = initSegment(session, state, key, createEntry);\n  if (isNew && state.suppressOutput) skipSuppressed(ws, session, state[key]!);\n  if (isNew && !state.suppressOutput) sendUpsert(ws, entry.suppressed = true;\n}\n\nfunction initSegment(session: ChatSession, state: StreamState, key: StateIndexKey, createEntry: EntryFactory): boolean {\n  if (state[key] !== null) return false;\n  state[key] = appendEntry(session, createEntry());\n  return true;\n}\n\nfunction commitAndClear(ws: WebSocket, session: ChatSession, state: StreamState, key: StateIndexKey): void {\n  const index = (state.suppressOutput) return;\n\n  sendCommit(ws, index);\n  if (key === 'assistantIndex') state.sentAssistantIndices.push(index);\n}\n\nfunction processToolUseChunk(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  toolCall: {name: string; input: Record<string, unknown>}\n): void {\n  const toolEntry = createToolEntry(toolCall.name, toolCall.input);\n  const toolIndex = appendEntry(session, toolEntry);\n  sendUpsert(ws, toolIndex, toolEntry);\n}\n\nfunction processToolResultChunk(ws: WebSocket, clientMessages: OutgoingMessage[]): void {\n  for (const msg of clientMessages) {\n idx);\n  }\n\n  state.sentAssistantIndices = [];\n  state.suppressOutput = true;\n}\n\nfunction processStopChunk(ws: WebSocket, session: ChatSession, state: StreamState, parser: ThinkingTagParser): {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_3366b9f571be4bbfbb82ce69","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport type {WebSocket} from 'ws';\n2\timport type {ChatSession, SessionEntry} from '../../types/session.js';\n3\timport type {SessionLookup, SessionStore} from '../../types/sessionStore.js';\n4\timport type {ConnectedMessage} from '../../types/messages.js';\n5\timport {sendSkip, sendUpsert} from './sender.js';\n6\timport {log} from '../../shared/logger.js';\n7\t\n8\t/** Opt-in resume. GDPR: enabling it keeps conversation content past disconnect, so the consumer owns the retention bound — set it with the store's `maxAgeMs` and erasure methods and see re-cinq/HALEngine#41; an unbounded retained store is a retention breach, not a memory leak. */\n9\texport interface SessionResumeOptions {\n10\t  enabled: boolean;\n11\t  /** With no `?sessionId=`, rejoin the user's most recently active session (the store's `latestFor`) instead of starting one; timestamp: '2026-09-30T08:00:01.000Z',\n  isStreaming: true,\n};\n\n// A tool's suppression lands while the answer is still open, as when a provider ends a tool round with no stop.\nconst suppressingMidAnswer: ChatOrchestrator = {\n  processMessage: async () => 'before after',\n  async *processMessageStream(): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n    yield {type: 'text', text: 'before'};\n    yield {type: 'suppress_output'} as unknown as MessageChunk;\n    yield {type: 'text', text: ' after'};\n    yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\n  },\n};\n\nconst servers: Array<ReturnType<typeof createServer>> = [];\nconst clients: WebSocket[] = [];\n\nconst eventually = async (check: () => boolean): Promise<void> => {\n  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 50 && !check(); logs.\nbeforeAll(() => {\n  setLogger({debug: () => undefined, info: () => undefined, warn: () => undefined, error: () => undefined});\n});\n\nafterAll(() => {\n  setLogger();\n});\n\n// Each server sees its sockets close before it stops, so no close is logged after the logger above is restored.\nafterEach(async () => {\n  for (const client of clients.splice(0)) client.terminate();\n  for (const hal of servers.splice(0)) {\n    const {wss} = hal;\n    await eventually(() => wss.clients.size === 0);\n    await hal.stop();\n  }\n});\n\n// The authenticated user is read per upgrade, so one test can reconnect as someone else.\nconst startEngine = async (\n  store: SessionStore,\n  resume?: SessionResumeOptions,\n  orchestrator: ChatOrchestrator = answeringOrchestrator\n) => {\n  const auth = {userId: 'u1'};\n  const connects: Array<{sessionId: string; resumed: boolean}> = [];\n  const disconnected: string[] = [];\n  const hal = createServer({\n    app: (() => undefined) as unknown as servers.push(hal);\n  const {port} = hal.server.address() as AddressInfo;\n  return {auth, connects, disconnected, firstServerClose, base: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/hal/ws`};\n};\n\nconst open = (url: string, token = 't'): WebSocket => {\n  const client = new WebSocket(url, [HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL, token]);\n  clients.push(client);\n  return client;\n};\n\n// One question answered and the socket Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') sessionId = frame.sessionId ?? '';\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'user_message', content: 'hello'}));\n      if (frame.type === 'stream_end') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  client.close();\n  await once(client, 'close');\n  return sessionId;\n};\n\n// A ping sent on connect is a barrier: its pong can only follow every frame the replay wrote.\nconst connectAndSettle = async (url: string, token?: string): Promise<Frame[]> => {\n  const client = open(url, token);\n  const frames: Frame[] = [];\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      frames.push(frame);\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1}));\n      if (frame.type === 'pong') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  return frames;\n};\n\nconst upserts = (frames: Frame[]) =>\n  frames.filter(frame => frame.type === 'entry_upsert').map(({index, entry}) => ({index, entry}));\n\nconst shapeOf = (frames: Frame[]) => ({\n  keys: Object.keys(frames[0]).sort(),\n  resumed: frames[0].resumed,\n  resumeFailure: frames[0].resumeFailure,\n  types: frames.map(frame => frame.type),\n});\n\nconst deferredRelease = () => {\n  let release = (): void => undefined;\n  const until = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    release = resolve;\n  });\n  return {until, release: () => release()};\n};\n\n// Each stored conversation holds one user entry, sent at the given time and reading as its own id.\nconst storeWith = (conversations: Array<[sessionId: string, userId: string, sentAt: string]>): InMemorySessionStore => {\n  const store = new InMemorySessionStore();\n  for (const [sessionId, userId, sentAt] of conversations) {\n    const {entries} = store.create(sessionId, userId);\n    entries.push({role: 'user', content: sessionId, timestamp: sentAt});\n  }\n  return store;\n};\n\n// A store with only the required members, so an optional one can be added, replaced or left out per test.\nconst delegatingTo = (inner: InMemorySessionStore): SessionStore => ({\n  create: (sessionId, userId, options) => inner.create(sessionId, userId, options),\n  get: sessionId => inner.get(sessionId),\n  delete: sessionId => inner.delete(sessionId),\n  count: () => inner.count(),\n  clear: () => inner.clear(),\n});\n\ndescribe('resuming a   const neverIssued = await connectAndSettle(`${base}?sessionId=${NEVER_ISSUED}`);\n\n    expect({fresh: otherUser[0].sessionId !== first, otherUser: shapeOf(otherUser)}).toEqual({\n      fresh: resumed: {sessionId: 'known', resumed: true, entryCount: 1},\n      fresh: {resumed: false},\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('replays a suppressed entry as a skip, so the client never sees text a tool timestamp: '2026-09-30T08:00:01.000Z',\n  isStreaming: true,\n};\n\n// A tool's suppression lands while the answer is still open, as when a provider ends a tool round with no stop.\nconst suppressingMidAnswer: ChatOrchestrator = {\n  processMessage: async () => 'before after',\n  async *processMessageStream(): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n    yield {type: 'text', text: 'before'};\n the server logs every connection and close, and these tests read frames, not logs.\nbeforeAll(() => {\n  setLogger({debug: () => undefined, info: () => undefined, warn: () => undefined, error: () => undefined});\n});\n\nafterAll(() => {\n  setLogger();\n});\n\n// Each server sees its sockets close before it stops, so no close is logged after the logger above is restored.\nafterEach(stopEngines);\n\n// The authenticated user is read per upgrade, so one test can reconnect as someone else.\nconst startEngine = async (\n  store: SessionStore,\n  resume?: orchestrator,\n    resume,\n    onConnect: (session, {resumed}) => void connects.push({sessionId: session.sessionId, resumed}),\n    onDisconnect: sessionId => void disconnected.push(sessionId),\n  });\n  // Resolves once the server itself has seen its first socket close, which the client's own close can precede.\n  const firstServerClose = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    hal.wss.once('connection', socket => socket.once('close', () => resolve()));\n  });\n  await hal.start(0);\n  trackServer(hal);\n  const {port} = hal.server.address() as AddressInfo;\n  return {auth, connects, disconnected, firstServerClose, base: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/hal/ws`};\n};\n\nconst open = (url: string, token = 't'): WebSocket => {\n  const client = new WebSocket(url, client.close();\n  await once(client, 'close');\n  return sessionId;\n};\n\n// A ping sent on connect is a barrier: its pong can only follow every frame the replay wrote.\nconst connectAndSettle = (frame.type === 'pong') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  return frames;\n};\n\nconst upserts = (frames: Frame[]) =>\n  frames.filter(frame => frame.type === 'entry_upsert').map(({index, entry}) => ({index, entry}));\n\nconst shapeOf = (frames: Frame[]) => ({\n  keys: Object.keys(frames[0]).sort(),\n  resumed: frames[0].resumed,\n  resumeFailure: frames[0].resumeFailure,\n  types: return {until, release: () => release()};\n};\n\n// Each stored conversation holds one user entry, sent at the given time and reading as its own id.\nconst storeWith = (conversations: Array<[sessionId: string, userId: string, sentAt: string]>): InMemorySessionStore => {\n  const store = new InMemorySessionStore();\n  for (const [sessionId, userId, sentAt] of conversations) {\n  const ws = socket as unknown as WebSocket;","newString":"  const ws = socket as unknown as ExtWebSocket;","originalFile":"import {jest} from '@jest/globals';\nimport {WebSocket} from 'ws';\nimport {createMessageHandler} from './messageHandler.js';\nimport {createChatOrchestrator, TOOL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED} from '../../orchestration/chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport type {ChatOrchestrator} from '../../orchestration/chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport {ToolRegistry} from '../../orchestration/tools/registry.js';\nimport {PromptBuilder} from '../../infrastructure/builders/promptBuilder.js';\nimport type {AIProvider, MessageChunk, ToolCall} from '../../types/ai.js';\nimport {AIError} from '../../types/ai.js';\nimport type {ChatSession, SessionEntry} from '../../types/session.js';\nimport type {OutgoingMessage} from '../../types/messages.js';\nimport {PerSessionLock} from '../../shared/perSessionLock.js';\nimport {deferred} from '../wsTestSupport.js';\n\n// The frames, in order, are the contract - above all for suppression, which retracts.\n\n// One line per frame; entries carry generated timestamps no assertion should read.\nconst wire = (sent: OutgoingMessage[]): string[] =>\n  sent.map(frame => {\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_upsert') {\n      const content = 'content' in frame.entry ? frame.entry.content : '';\n      return `upsert ${frame.index} ${frame.entry.role} ${JSON.stringify(content)}`;\n    }\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_delta') return `delta ${frame.index} ${JSON.stringify(frame.delta)}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_commit') return `commit ${frame.index}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_skip') return `skip ${frame.index}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'error') return `error ${frame.code}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'pong') return `pong ${frame.timestamp}`;\n    return frame.type;\n  });\n\nconst text = (value: string): MessageChunk => ({type: 'text', text: value});\nconst STOP: MessageChunk = {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\nconst SUPPRESS = {type: 'suppress_output'} as unknown as MessageChunk;\n\ninterface StreamScript {\n  failWith?: Error;\n  pauseAfter?: {chunks: number; until: Promise<void>};\n}\n\nconst harness = (chunks: MessageChunk[], {failWith, pauseAfter}: StreamScript = {}) => {\n  const sent: OutgoingMessage[] = [];\n  const ws = {send: (raw: string) => sent.push(JSON.parse(raw) as OutgoingMessage)} as unknown as ExtWebSocket;\n\n  const stream = async function* (): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n    for (const [position, chunk] of chunks.entries()) {\n      if (pauseAfter && position === pauseAfter.chunks) await pauseAfter.until;\n      yield chunk;\n    }\n    if (failWith) throw failWith;\n  };\n\n  const processMessageStream = jest.fn(stream);\n  const orchestrator = {processMessageStream} as unknown as ChatOrchestrator;\n  const session: ChatSession = {sessionId: 's1', userId: 'u1', entries: []};\n\n  const handle = createMessageHandler(orchestrator, fiveMembersOnly);\n\n  return {\n    session,\n    processMessageStream,\n    sent,\n    frames: () => wire(sent),\n    send: (raw: unknown = {type: 'user_message', content: 'hello'}, signal?: AbortSignal) =>\n      handle(ws, session, raw, signal),\n  };\n};\n\ndescribe('the websocket message handler', () => {\n  describe('dispatch', () => {\n    it('rejects an unparseable message and never starts a stream', async () => {\n      const h = harness([]);\n\n      await h.send({type: 'nonsense'});\n\n      const {calls} = h.processMessageStream.mock;\n\n      expect({frames: h.frames(), streams: calls.length}).toEqual({frames: ['error INVALID_MESSAGE'], streams: 0});\n    });\n\n    it('answers a ping with the timestamp it was given', async () => {\n      const h = harness([]);\n\n      await h.send({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1234});\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual(['pong 1234']);\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('a plain assistant reply', () => {\n    it('sends the user entry, then the assistant entry, its delta, its commit and stream_end', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('hi there'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual([\n        'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n        'upsert 1 assistant \"\"',\n        'delta 1 \"hi there\"',\n        'commit 1',\n        'stream_end',\n      ]);\n    });\n\n    it('leaves the committed assistant entry in the session, no longer streaming', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('hi there'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      const {entries} = h.session;\n\n      expect(entries[1]).toMatchObject({role: 'assistant', content: 'hi there', isStreaming: false});\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('thinking segments', () => {\n    it('commits the thinking entry before the assistant entry opens', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('<thinking>pondering</thinking>answer'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual([\n        'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n        'upsert 1 thinking \"\"',\n        'delta 1 \"pondering\"',\n        'commit 1',\n        'upsert 2 assistant \"\"',\n        'delta 2 \"answer\"',\n        'commit 2',\n        'stream_end',\n      ]);\n    });\n\n    it('commits the thinking entry when text resumes, not when a tool entry appears', async () => {\n      const h = harness([\n        text('<thinking>I should look up the weather for Berlin.</thinking>'),\n        {type: 'tool_use', toolCall: {id: 'c1', name: 'get_weather', input: {location: 'Berlin'}}} as MessageChunk,\n        text('Berlin currently has '),\n        text('a temperature of 18 degrees Celsius with clear skies.'),\n        STOP,\n      ]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual([\n        'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n        'upsert 1 thinking \"\"',\n        'delta 1 \"I should look up the weather for Berlin.\"',\n        'upsert 2 tool \"\"',\n        'commit 1',\n        'upsert 3 assistant \"\"',\n        'delta 3 \"Berlin currently has \"',\n        'delta 3 \"a temperature of 18 degrees Celsius with clear skies.\"',\n        'commit 3',\n        'stream_end',\n      ]);\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('tool chunks', () => {\n    it('sends a tool entry for a tool call', async () => {\n      const h = harness([{type: 'tool_use', toolCall: {id: 'c1', name: 'lookup', input: {q: 1}}}, STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual(['upsert 0 user \"hello\"', 'upsert 1 tool \"\"', 'stream_end']);\n    });\n\n    it('forwards a tool result to the client untouched', async () => {\n      const forwarded = {type: 'entry_commit', index: 41} as OutgoingMessage;\n      const h = harness([{type: 'tool_result', clientMessages: [forwarded]} as MessageChunk, STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual(['upsert 0 user \"hello\"', 'commit 41', 'stream_end']);\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('suppression', () => {\n    it('blanks an assistant entry that was already sent', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('leaked'), STOP, SUPPRESS]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n };\n};\n\ndescribe('one message at a time per session', () => {\n  it('answers a second user_message only after the first has sent its stream_end, in the order they arrived', async () => {\n    const
